http_semantics.note: The killing request is spec-legal (both parameters >= 1, no documented maximum), so the 2xx-business-code vs 4xx question does not apply: the server returned NO HTTP response at all (connection aborted mid-request) and then the process died — /healthz unreachable, docker OOMKilled exit 137. The forbidden outcome is the service death itself, not a misrouted error code.

contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check, honest branch = 'value genuinely compliant': the observed values (limit=1000000, group_size=1000000) are INSIDE the quote's constraint domain and satisfy its only clauses (both >= 1; no maximum is documented in the contract text nor in the versioned OpenAPI artifact), so the OOM does not violate this assertion's own words — api_violates_assertion=false is the compliant-value branch, not the wrong-constraint-cited branch. The phenomenon (request-triggered service death on spec-legal values) has no covering constraint in this contract: the resource_bound_constraints block carries the inferred never-crash pattern only for shard_number, offsets/pairs sample+limit, and facet limit (qdrant_resource_shard_number_001, qdrant_resource_offsets_sample_001, qdrant_resource_offsets_limit_001, qdrant_resource_pairs_sample_001, qdrant_resource_pairs_limit_001, qdrant_resource_facet_limit_001) — NOT for points+query+groups limit/group_size; the cited range constraint is the nearest mechanical anchor and its letter does not forbid the observed outcome. Expected consequence for the auditor: mechanical A likely NEUTRAL on this constraint; the resource_bound/robustness judgment (R11-class parallel, docker OOM corroboration, source-level unguarded multiplication) is perspective-B territory. candidates.jsonl constraint_id field was an empty string for this defect_id; the constraint was resolved via the attack string ('strategy6 resource x qdrant_range_points_query_groups_001') and the script header (constraint_ids + docstring quoting the assertion verbatim).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /collections/{name}/points/query/groups -> src/actix/api/query_api.rs:199 query_points_groups (actix_web_validator::Json<QueryGroupsRequest> runs #[validate(range(min=1))] on limit/group_size — the only check; NO max; usize accepts any JSON integer >= 1) -> convert_query_groups_request_from_rest (query_requests_rest.rs:70-88; unwrap_or defaults 10/3; no clamping) -> do_query_point_groups (src/common/query.rs:320) -> GroupRequest::from (group_by.rs:267, plain usize passthrough) -> toc.group (lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/point_ops.rs:233 — RBAC check only) -> GroupBy::new(...).execute() (grouping/builder.rs:38/71 — no validation) -> into_query_group_request (group_by.rs:82; QueryGroupRequest{group_size, groups: limit}) -> group_by() (group_by.rs:310) -> GroupsAggregator::new(request.groups, request.group_size, ...) at group_by.rs:323 — FIRST statement before any search: all_ids AHashSet::with_capacity(groups * group_size) = with_capacity(1_000_000_000_000) for 24-byte ExtendedPointId elements, plus three 1e6-capacity maps (groups, full_groups, group_best_scores) -> eager multi-TB reservation inside a 2 GiB cgroup -> process death (docker: oom -> die, exitCode=137, State.OOMKilled=true) before any HTTP response (client sees RemoteDisconnected; /healthz then unreachable). Secondary products on the same path if construction were survived: group_by.rs:155 request.limit = groups * group_size (1e12 into the source query) and group_by.rs:547 shard_prefetch.limit *= group_size (recursive prefetch multiplication); per-group add_point also does AHashMap::with_capacity(max_group_size)=1e6 per group hit (aggregator.rs:72). No upper-bound, resource, or feasibility check exists anywhere on the path; callers never re-validate; gRPC face is wider still (Option<u64>). Whole-tree search for caps on limit/group_size found none (the only range(max=...) resource guards in the codebase are candidates_limit 16384 'artificial maximum' schema.rs:748-752, VectorParams.size 65536). Maintainer tests: grouping_test.rs exercises limit 4/500 (big_limit_groups) and zero boundaries — the 1e6+ resource region is untested upstream.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Eager preallocation driven by the unchecked product of the two documented caps: GroupsAggregator::new's all_ids AHashSet::with_capacity(groups * group_size) — with limit=1e6 x group_size=1e6 a 1e12-element capacity reservation (>= 2^40 buckets of 24-byte ExtendedPointId plus control bytes; tens of terabytes) inside a 2 GiB container — OOM-kills the process (docker State.OOMKilled=true, exit 137) before any HTTP response, corroborated 3/3 deterministic executions; the exact terminal step (control-table page-touch triggering the cgroup OOM killer vs allocation-failure abort) is not distinguishable from client-side evidence alone, but every variant is request-triggered service death on spec-legal input — the R11-class resource_bound phenomenon. The contract's inferred resource_bound pattern covers shard_number / offsets / pairs / facet but was never extracted for query-groups limit x group_size, which is the assertion-coverage gap recorded in contract_grounding.note.
